title: Trying to convince people you’re right is underrated
gist: Yglesias argues people should judge information sources by whether they casually make easily falsifiable claims rather than by friend/enemy alignment, citing Erick Erickson's false claim that AI-safety advocates are the same people as climate and anti-nuclear 'doomers'; he also argues persuasion has gone missing from progressive political thinking, in the context of a Talarico vs. Paxton Senate race.

insights.claim: Rather than aligning with sources by political tribe, people should discount sources that casually make false statements about easily verifiable facts.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Practical heuristic for filtering commentary on contested issues like AI policy.
insights.quote: What you ought to do instead is try to see which people casually toss off false statements about things that are easily verifiable.

insights.claim: For almost any widely held political view, a large share of its holders are ignorant or sloppy reasoners, so agreement with a position is a poor signal of source reliability.

insights.claim: Popping off with a mistake is forgivable, but persisting after being corrected by better-informed people is a disqualifying trait in a source.

insights.so_what: Track whether commentators update when corrected before trusting them.

insights.claim: Conservatives aligning with the White House's regulatory skepticism on AI safety are claiming that AI-risk advocates are the same people as climate doomers and anti-nuclear activists.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Shows the White House stance against AI-safety regulation is being reinforced by partisan framing—lower odds of federal AI safety rules.
insights.quote: The nuclear power doomers became the climate doomers and now they’re the AI doomers.

insights.claim: Yglesias says the claim that AI-safety advocates are former climate doomers is false because the effective altruist community and the climate movement have been antagonistic, as EAs rejected apocalyptic climate narratives.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: AI-safety coalition is distinct from climate/anti-nuclear activism; don't model its politics as a green-movement extension.

insights.claim: A dispute between Will Stancil and Parker Molloy centers on whether trans activists should work to reduce support for James Talarico over his trans stance even if it risks a Paxton win and a 50/50 Senate.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias

insights.claim: Yglesias argues the concept of persuading people you are correct has gone weirdly missing from much progressive thinking about the political system.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Suggests a push toward persuasion-oriented, more moderate Democratic messaging.
insights.quote: the big thing that has gone weirdly missing from a lot of progressive thinking about the political system is the concept of “persuade people that you are correct.”
